$comment: Curated starter dataset for ECHOES. Every record points at a real, citable source. Coordinates are approximate place centroids captured during curation and are flagged via coordinateAccuracy; they must be re-validated against an authoritative source before being treated as survey-grade. 'coverage' records which information dimensions were actually found in the sources that were checked — it is evidence of what the checked datasets contain, NOT a claim that a place's history is unknown.

places.name: Freedom Park Lagos
places.address: Old Prison Ground, Broad Street, Lagos Island, Lagos
places.summary: A public park and memorial built on the grounds of the former Broad Street Prison.
places.history: Freedom Park occupies the site of the former Broad Street Prison, which operated during the colonial period. The prison was closed and the site was redeveloped as a memorial park, opening in 2010. It now hosts concerts, theatre, art exhibitions and cultural events, and is also discussed as a site of memory connected to the colonial penal system.

coordinates.evidence: Location recorded in OpenStreetMap and cross-checked against the published street address.

encyclopedicArticle.evidence: English Wikipedia article exists and was retrieved.

structuredFacts.evidence: No Wikidata entity for the park itself was confirmed during curation; structured statements (founding date, ownership) could not be verified.

image.evidence: No openly licensed image from the checked sources was confirmed for reuse.

citations.evidence: Community members frequently describe events here; those accounts are not yet attached with citations.

communityStory.evidence: No moderated community story has been submitted for this place yet.

verifiedExperience.evidence: No verified guided experience is currently listed.

places.name: National Museum Lagos
places.summary: Nigeria's principal national museum, holding archaeology and ethnography collections.
places.history: The National Museum in Onikan was established in the 1950s and holds one of the country's main collections of archaeology, ethnography and traditional art, including Nok terracotta pieces. It is administered by the National Commission for Museums and Monuments.

sources.title: National Commission for Museums and Monuments

coordinates.evidence: Coordinates cross-checked against the Onikan location in OpenStreetMap.

encyclopedicArticle.evidence: English Wikipedia article exists and was retrieved.

structuredFacts.evidence: Collection inventory and opening-hours statements are not available from an open structured source.

image.evidence: Openly licensed photographs of the museum exterior are published on Wikimedia Commons.

citations.evidence: Collection scope is documented in the encyclopedia article's cited sources.

communityStory.evidence: Two community accounts were submitted and are queued for moderation.

verifiedExperience.evidence: No verified guided experience is currently listed.

places.name: Cathedral Church of Christ, Lagos
places.summary: Anglican cathedral on the Lagos Island waterfront, in its present building since the 1940s.
places.history: The Cathedral Church of Christ on Marina is the seat of the Anglican diocese of Lagos. Earlier church buildings on the site date to the nineteenth century; the present cathedral was consecrated in the 1940s. Its bells and organ are part of its documented musical history.

sources.title: Cathedral Church of Christ, Lagos — Wikipedia

encyclopedicArticle.evidence: English Wikipedia article exists and was retrieved.

structuredFacts.evidence: Consecration date and denomination are stated consistently across checked sources.

image.evidence: Openly licensed exterior photographs are published on Wikimedia Commons.

citations.evidence: Architectural and musical history are cited in the encyclopedia article.

communityStory.evidence: No moderated community story has been submitted for this place yet.

verifiedExperience.evidence: No verified guided experience is currently listed.

places.name: Tafawa Balewa Square
places.summary: A large public square on Lagos Island associated with Nigeria's independence ceremonies.
places.history: Tafawa Balewa Square is a major public square on Lagos Island, used for national ceremonies and public gatherings. It is widely associated with Nigeria's independence celebrations in 1960. The square takes its current name from Nigeria's first prime minister.

encyclopedicArticle.evidence: English Wikipedia article exists and was retrieved.

structuredFacts.evidence: Checked sources differ on the date the square was renamed; the discrepancy is unresolved and flagged.

image.evidence: No openly licensed image from the checked sources was confirmed for reuse.

citations.evidence: Some event claims in circulating accounts lack citations.

communityStory.evidence: No moderated community story has been submitted for this place yet.

verifiedExperience.evidence: No verified guided experience is currently listed.

places.name: Iga Idunganran (Oba's Palace)
places.summary: The palace of the Oba of Lagos, with documented origins in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
places.history: Iga Idunganran is the palace of the Oba of Lagos on Lagos Island. Documented origins are usually traced to the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, and the palace was substantially rebuilt in the nineteenth century. It remains an active seat of traditional authority and a cultural reference point for Lagos Island communities.

encyclopedicArticle.evidence: The article exists but is short and covers the reconstruction period unevenly.

structuredFacts.evidence: Succession dates and building phases are not available from a single consistent structured source.

image.evidence: Openly licensed photographs are published on Wikimedia Commons.

citations.evidence: Oral accounts of the palace's history are important here but are not yet recorded with attribution.

communityStory.evidence: One community account has been submitted and is queued for moderation.

verifiedExperience.evidence: No verified guided experience is currently listed.

places.name: Brazilian Quarter (Popo Aguda)
places.summary: A historic island neighbourhood shaped by nineteenth-century returnees from Brazil.
places.history: Popo Aguda, the 'Brazilian Quarter', is a historic district on Lagos Island settled in the nineteenth century by returned Africans from Brazil, known locally as Agudas. The area is known for its distinctive architecture and for crafts such as masonry and carpentry associated with those families.

coordinates.evidence: Neighbourhood boundary approximate; centroid cross-checked in OpenStreetMap.

encyclopedicArticle.evidence: English Wikipedia article 'Brazilian Quarters' exists and was retrieved.

structuredFacts.evidence: No structured entity was confirmed for the quarter as a cultural heritage area.

image.evidence: No openly licensed image of the surviving architecture was confirmed for reuse.

citations.evidence: Family histories are largely oral and not yet recorded with consent and attribution.

places.name: Jaekel House
places.address: Nigerian Railway Corporation compound, Ebute Metta, Lagos
places.summary: A restored colonial-era railway residence in Ebute Metta, now a heritage site and museum.
places.history: Jaekel House is a restored colonial-era residence within the Nigerian Railway Corporation compound at Ebute Metta. It is used as a museum and heritage venue and is associated with the history of the Lagos railway and its staff.

coordinates.evidence: Coordinates fall within the railway compound per OpenStreetMap.

image.evidence: Openly licensed photographs are published on Wikimedia Commons.

citations.evidence: Restoration history is documented but not fully cited in open sources.

places.name: New Afrika Shrine
places.summary: A live music venue in Ikeja associated with Afrobeat and the Kuti family.
places.history: The New Afrika Shrine is a live music venue in Ikeja associated with the Kuti family and with Afrobeat. It succeeds the original Afrika Shrine, which was associated with Fela Anikulapo Kuti, and hosts regular live performances.

places.name: Kalakuta Museum
places.summary: The former residence of Fela Anikulapo Kuti, now a museum of his life and Afrobeat.
places.history: Kalakuta Museum occupies the former Lagos residence of musician and activist Fela Anikulapo Kuti — the house associated with the Kalakuta Republic period. It presents his personal effects and documents the history of Afrobeat. It operates as a museum and cultural site.

places.history: The National Theatre at Iganmu is a large performing-arts complex associated with Nigeria's national cultural festivals. It opened in the 1970s and remains a major architectural landmark on the Lagos mainland.

places.history: Terra Kulture is a cultural centre, bookshop and theatre on Victoria Island. It programmes Nigerian literature, visual art and stage productions, and has been a venue for language and arts events in Lagos.

places.summary: A private art gallery in Lekki founded by artist Nike Davies-Okundaye.
places.history: Nike Art Gallery in Lekki was founded by the artist and textile designer Nike Davies-Okundaye. It presents Nigerian painting, sculpture, textiles and adire work across several floors, and runs workshops in traditional crafts.

places.history: The Lekki Conservation Centre is a nature reserve on the Lekki peninsula, managed by the Nigerian Conservation Foundation. It is known for its canopy walkway and for conservation and environmental education programmes.

places.summary: A major textile and trading market on Lagos Island.
places.history: Balogun Market is one of the largest trading markets on Lagos Island, known particularly for fabrics, textiles and tailoring materials. It forms part of the dense commercial district around Balogun and Martins streets.

places.name: Makoko
places.summary: A waterfront settlement on Lagos Lagoon with a long-established fishing community.
places.history: Makoko is a waterfront settlement on Lagos Lagoon. It developed from a fishing community associated with migration from the Badagry area, and many homes and businesses sit on stilts over the water. It is a community with its own schools and institutions and is frequently discussed in debates about urban development and displacement.

coordinates.evidence: Settlement centroid approximate; cross-checked in OpenStreetMap.

encyclopedicArticle.evidence: English Wikipedia article exists and was retrieved.

structuredFacts.evidence: Population figures vary widely between checked sources and should not be treated as reliable.

image.evidence: Openly licensed photographs are published on Wikimedia Commons.

citations.evidence: Community history is largely oral; consent-based recording has not yet been completed.

communityStory.evidence: Community submissions require the sensitive-content review path before publication.

verifiedExperience.evidence: No verified guided experience is currently listed. Any experience here must be community-owned and consent-based.

places.name: First Storey Building, Badagry
places.summary: A nineteenth-century building in Badagry associated with early Christian missionary activity.
places.history: The building in Badagry known as the First Storey Building is associated with nineteenth-century Christian missionary activity in the area, including the work of the Church Missionary Society. It is frequently described as the first two-storey building in Nigeria, and is preserved as a heritage site with a small museum.

sources.title: First Storey Building in Nigeria — Wikipedia

encyclopedicArticle.evidence: English Wikipedia article exists and was retrieved.

structuredFacts.evidence: Construction dates differ between checked sources; the 'first storey building' claim itself is contested in the literature and is flagged as such.

image.evidence: Openly licensed photographs are published on Wikimedia Commons.

citations.evidence: The building's interpretive claims need stronger citation.

communityStory.evidence: No moderated community story has been submitted for this place yet.

verifiedExperience.evidence: No verified guided experience is currently listed.

places.name: Badagry Heritage Museum
places.summary: A museum in Badagry documenting the history of the transatlantic slave trade in the region.
places.history: The Badagry Heritage Museum documents the history of the transatlantic slave trade as it affected Badagry and the wider Bight of Benin. It is housed in a former colonial administrative building and forms part of the heritage sites visited along the Badagry route, which includes the point of no return.

encyclopedicArticle.evidence: The article is brief relative to the site's significance.

structuredFacts.evidence: No structured entity was confirmed for the museum.

image.evidence: Images exist but licensing for reuse was not confirmed for all of them.

citations.evidence: Sensitive subject matter requires careful, well-cited interpretation.

communityStory.evidence: Submissions on this subject follow the sensitive-content review path.
